summary.text: James Sanders Jr. is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for New York State Senate District 10, which includes parts of Queens, and is running unopposed for re-election.
A Marine veteran from the Rockaways, he worked for Congressman Floyd Flake, led a Queens school board and served on the New York City Council before his election to the State Senate in 2012.
He chairs the Senate Committee on Banks.

paragraphs.text: Sanders was born and raised in Hammel Houses, a public housing development in the Rockaways, in Southeast Queens.
He graduated from Far Rockaway High School and earned a bachelor's degree in history, with a specialization in African-American studies, from Brooklyn College in 1984.
He served in the U.S. Marine Corps, and his Senate biography describes him as a Marine veteran.
Before entering elected office, Sanders worked in the political operation of U.S. Representative Floyd H. Flake.
He served as President of Queens School Board District 27, becoming the first African-American elected to lead the board.
He was elected to the New York City Council representing District 31 in 2001 and served until 2012, and became the first African-American chair of the Council's Economic Development Committee.
Sanders was first elected to the State Senate in 2012, took office on January 1, 2013, and is now serving his sixth term, according to his Senate biography and Ballotpedia.

He chairs the Senate Committee on Banks and the Select Majority Task Force on Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises, and he is also a member of the Commerce, Economic Development and Small Business, Insurance, Labor, Racing, Gaming and Wagering, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.
He serves as Vice President of the National Black Caucus of State Legislators.
